chunks: 5227 - Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Hishām ibn Sālim, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abū ʿUbaydah, who said:

I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a blind man who intentionally gouged out the eye of a sighted person. He said: “O Abū ʿUbaydah, the intentional act of a blind man is like a mistake; in this case there is diyyah from his wealth. If he has no wealth, then the diyyah for that is upon the Imam, and the right of a Muslim is not to be invalidated.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: financial compensation owed for bodily injury
key_terms.الْخَطَإِ: mistake or accidental harm in legal classification
key_terms.حَقُّ مُسْلِمٍ: the legal right due to a Muslim that must not be nullified
key_terms.عَلَى الْإِمَامِ: the liability falls upon the Imam if the offender lacks means
key_terms.عَمْدُ الْأَعْمَى: the intentional act of a blind person, treated here under a special legal ruling
key_terms.مِنْ مَالِهِ: to be paid from his own property or wealth

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a blind man intentionally injures someone and has no wealth to pay the diyyah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that the deliberate bodily injury committed by a blind person is treated like an accidental act in terms of liability. Compensation is paid as diyyah from his property, and if he has no wealth, the Imam assumes responsibility so that the injured Muslim’s right is not lost.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5227 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim from Ammar Al-Sabaṭi from Abu Ubaydah, who said:

I asked Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about a blind man who intentionally gouged out the eye of a sighted person.
Imam (as) said: "O' Abu Ubaydah, the intentional act of a blind man is treated like a mistake (khaṭaʾ). The blood money (diyyah) must be paid from his wealth. If he has no wealth, then the diyyah is upon the Imam. The right of a Muslim must not be invalidated."
